sentences.text: Andy Burnham has hailed a deal between Denmark and the US to "strengthen security in the Arctic" after the two countries resolved a months-long feud over Greenland.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The UK prime minister and his Danish counterpart Mette Frederiksen "welcomed the US's commitment to the region" in a call on Sunday morning, Downing Street said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Nato previously said the agreement would help stabilise the region, as Trump declared Denmark would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory in the Arctic.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Burnham's comments come as he is expected to meet Trump for the first time at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York this week.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control' The agreement comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns, citing its strategic location for defence purposes as well as its mineral wealth.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: No text of the agreement has been released, but Trump said in a Truth Social post the deal came with "no cost to the United States" and meant it could "do what is necessary" to "secure and defend the security of Greenland".
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: He said it included a rule that no US adversary could maintain a military presence in Greenland or "make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval".
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: In a readout of Sunday's phone call, a No 10 spokesperson said Burnham and Frederiksen "welcomed the US's commitment to the region and underlined the strategic and shared importance of the High North for Euro-Atlantic security".
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: "So let Donald Trump try to pretend he's had a victory.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The truth is, Europe, Nato, countries like Canada stood up to him and won." Trump had tried for months to purchase or annex the semi-autonomous territory, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: In the wake of the deal, Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.

sentences.article_title: No criminality in death of three sisters who died in sea

sentences.article_title: No criminality in death of three sisters who died in sea

sentences.article_title: No criminality in death of three sisters who died in sea

sentences.article_title: No criminality in death of three sisters who died in sea

sentences.article_title: No criminality in death of three sisters who died in sea

sentences.text: "Our priority throughout has been uncovering the truth for the loved ones of Jane, Rebecca and Christina, because at this incident's core there has always been a grieving family coming to terms with an unthinkable tragedy and loss.

sentences.text: President Donald Trump has infused his ongoing feud with the White House press with a new level of acrimony.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Journalists from three major media outlets - CNN, Politico and MS Now - were denied access and had their press credentials confiscated on Saturday morning as they attempted to enter the White House grounds for work.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: As media watchdog organisations and the White House Correspondents Association cry foul, Trump appears set to press ahead with a sweeping effort to punish these outlets.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: In his Truth Social post announcing his decision on Friday, he said he was "banning" the organisations because "of their constant 'reporting' of fake news".
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: In remarks later that day, he complained that "something is wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories".
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: "If they want to write them, that's fine," he continued.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: "I don't have to let them into the people's house", he said, referring to the White House.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Journalists denied White House access after Trump banned some media outlets The president's frustration at the media, however, came after a week of setbacks in which major institutions handed him a series of losses across his agenda.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: First, the Supreme Court blocked his plan to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterms.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: This prompted Trump to lash out at the court's justices including those he had appointed.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: "These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court," he said.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: The Federal Reserve, the US central bank, then raised interest rates after Trump had spent months arguing they should be cut.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: This was followed by a judge ordering his administration to give 30 days' notice before making any changes to the Kennedy Center arts venue in Washington DC after the president warned it could be "ripped down".
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: These headlines, combined with approval ratings that recently sunk to record lows for his second term, suggest Trump is facing challenging political headwinds.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: His latest attack on the press, however, raises clear legal questions.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: The First Amendment to the US Constitution forbids Congress from "abridging" the freedom of the press.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: It is language that courts have long interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: All three targeted news outlets have promised to file lawsuits challenging Trump's decision.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Although the breadth of this move is unprecedented, it is far from the first time the Trump administration has attempted to limit or deny access to the White House to members of mainstream media outlets.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: In his first term, the administration revoked CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press credentials, setting off a legal battle that was ultimately resolved in the journalist's favour.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: It also temporarily suspended the pass of a reporter who had a heated argument with White House adviser Sebastian Gorka – a move that also was subsequently blocked by the courts.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: That dispute also led to a protracted - and yet to be fully resolved - legal battle, prompting the White House to change press pool rules to drop the guaranteed spot for all wire services.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Trump says ban on some news outlets from White House is "because they're fake news" The White House bans, however, represent a dramatic escalation.

sentences.text: The restrictions include access to the entirety of the White House grounds, not just the press pool.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: And they target entire news organisations, not just a single disfavoured correspondent.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: JLR suppliers say skills and factories could be redirected into aerospace and defence Major Jaguar Land Rover suppliers have urged the government to help automotive manufacturers move into aerospace and defence, warning that large-scale car production in the UK faces long-term decline.

sentences.text: In an open letter to the prime minister, chancellor and West Midlands Mayor Richard Parker, industry leaders argued Britain's automotive supply chain was "not in decline" but "in the wrong market".
sentences.article_title: JLR suppliers call for shift to aerospace

sentences.text: The intervention comes nearly a fortnight after JLR announced plans to cut 4,000 jobs.
sentences.article_title: JLR suppliers call for shift to aerospace

sentences.text: The Treasury said it recognised the uncertainty facing workers and was supporting the automotive sector through grants, lower energy costs and investment in electric vehicle production.
sentences.article_title: JLR suppliers call for shift to aerospace

sentences.text: JLR has its global headquarters in Coventry and plants in Solihull, Wolverhampton and Halewood.

sentences.text: Signatories to the letter said the redundancies were "the first visible crack" in a UK automotive supply chain supporting about 183,000 manufacturing jobs.

sentences.text: Speaking on BBC Politics Midlands, he said: "We want to take action today rather than wait for that to happen." Roberts argued there was a "very big opportunity" for manufacturers to redirect skills, factories and investment into the UK's expanding aerospace and defence sectors.

sentences.text: The department of justice said minister Naomi Long "remains deeply concerned surrounding compassionate temporary release of Gary Anderson and his subsequent absconding" The justice minister remains "deeply concerned" about the circumstances surrounding the temporary release of a convicted murderer.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: The NI Prison Service (NIPS) refused Gary Anderson permission to attend his father's funeral but that decision was quashed by the courts.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: Anderson was released on Monday from Maghaberry Prison to attend the funeral but absconded and remains at large.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: He is one of two brothers jailed for life in 2023 for the 2018 murder of Karol Kelly in Londonderry.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: The court service has now published the full 15 page judgement from the judicial review.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: It reveals the decision to refuse Anderson's request to attend the funeral was taken by the duty governor at Maghaberry Prison.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: But the judge found that that decision "was based upon inaccurate information which was material to the key issue of the potential risks posed by the applicant".
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: "The information which was considered was also materially disadvantageous to the applicant." That's a reference to an internal assessment of the likelihood of Anderson reoffending, which was wrongly recorded at a higher level than recorded in the internal system.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: A legal representative for the prison service admitted to the court that "information containing an increased score came, not from the duty governor's personal knowledge, but from a colleague.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: He invited the duty governor to review the decision but that offer was declined, in a move the judge described as "somewhat surprising".
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: Gary Anderson, who is serving a 15-year sentence for the murder of Karol Kelly, remains on the run In a statement, the Justice department said that "this opportunity was not communicated by legal representatives to those within NIPS who held responsibility for the decision".
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: He added "the failure to secure and take account of the correct risk assessment is unlawful".
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: The department said Minister Naomi Long "remains deeply concerned surrounding compassionate temporary release of Gary Anderson and his subsequent absconding".
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: Following a review of the case, further information emerged regarding the handling of the case.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: "The substantive decision to refuse Gary Anderson compassionate temporary release was, in my view, clearly correct.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: His subsequent absconding has only underlined the serious risk he presented.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: "However, that decision was catastrophically undermined by incorrect information, missing records and an extraordinary refusal to reconsider it when the court provided an opportunity to do so.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: "This was not a minor administrative error.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: The incorrect information went directly to the assessment of the risk posed by a convicted murderer and was expressly relied upon in refusing his release.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: "The decision collapsed because it relied upon materially incorrect information, the assessment supposedly supporting it could not be produced and the duty governor refused the opportunity to reconsider.
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: "The family of Karol Kelly and the wider public deserve the full truth, urgent accountability and firm action to ensure that this can never happen again."
sentences.article_title: Justice minister 'deeply concerned' over temporary release of convicted killer

sentences.text: M&S show during London Fashion Week September 2026 "I'm the first person to be like, 'It's from M&S, you need to get on to it,'" Farron Clark, a 26-year-old brand strategist tells me.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: According to Clark and others on social media, Marks & Spencer is becoming the hot place to shop for women under 35, while also keeping its core older audience happy too.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "For a long time M&S had this fusty reputation - it was less valued by younger people," says Chioma Nnadi, head of editorial content at British Vogue, who tells the BBC there is now a "fresh energy around the brand".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: And accompanying that fresh energy is a new marketing strategy, which includes hosting its first-ever London Fashion Week show on Friday, featuring a collection of outfits inspired by the brand's archive.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: Speaking ahead of the event at the Design Museum, the company's head of womenswear design, Lisa Illis, says they wanted to do this because of the "immediacy of seeing something and being able to own it and wear it, rather than waiting six months".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: For many, M&S is more synonymous with pig-shaped sweets than cutting-edge fashion, but its runway of 43 womenswear and 10 menswear looks did a lot to persuade people that the latter is where its true talent lies.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: Normally Fashion Week is about seeing what you'll be wearing six months from now, but this runway was full of colder weather fits, from opulent faux fur jackets and wrist cuffs, to satin jumpsuits and dresses in rich tones of navy, burgundy and brown.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: The catwalk featured a diverse range of models in age, size and gender, demonstrating the brand's desire to cater to a wide market.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: But there was certainly a concerted effort to attract the eye of younger shoppers with a fashion-forward approach to Christmas party staples like sequinned dresses, tasselled skirts and see-through lace tops.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: Womenswear and menswear collections at London Fashion Week are inspired by the M&S archive The retailer has been focusing on "newer styles and relevant trends" to attract younger customers, says Illis.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: But she says that this has been achieved without compromising on quality which is what keeps M&S's core audience on board.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "They have created a modern version of everything we know and love - cashmere staples, knitwear and the lingerie department," says Nnadi.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: Clark agrees that M&S has been nailing "funnel neck [styles] and barrel jeans, which are filtering down from high fashion".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: M&S has perhaps been fortunate to rebrand at a time when consumer habits are changing, as young shoppers consider buying capsule wardrobes - a smaller number of staple pieces that can be styled in a variety of ways.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: According to Clark, the idea of wear-it-once fast fashion has declined as people  "are looking for [foundational pieces] to rotate".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: This is something Perrie Sian, one of Britain's biggest fashion influencers, has also noticed.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: The 34-year-old tells the BBC: "The real height of fast fashion is behind us".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "As a group we've changed our shopping habits and M&S slots into that," she says.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "In my content and with lots of other creators we're showing people how to wear things in multiple ways, how to look after them." She added that she is noticing "people are willing to spend a little bit more" on wardrobe staples and items that "wash well and are made of cotton, not acrylic or polyester".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: Speaking on BBC Sounds podcast When It Hits The Fan, which she co-presents, Farzana Baduel, the president of the Chartered Institute of Public Relations, says it "hasn't always been rosy for M&S" and that past mis-steps had often led to the company being "absolutely hammered in the media".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "M&S fashion, which for a while sat there like a bit of a sleepy Bagpuss on the British retail mantlepiece, has had quite a glow-up," Baduel says.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: During the Covid pandemic M&S struggled, but returned to growth in 2022-2023, with its fashion, home and beauty market share reaching 9.6%.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: This again increased in 2023-2024 to 10%, and 10.5% in 2024-2025.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: But the business took a big hit in 2025 due to a cyber attack , which left shoppers unable to use its website and app and affected stock in stores too.

sentences.text: Nnadi says M&S has been investing heavily in its retail spaces in recent years, focusing on "accessible luxury" with stores that feel "welcoming, new and fresh".
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: And that's something Clark has noticed too.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "Getting an iced coffee and having a walk around M&S with my friends is the perfect Saturday," she says.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "I'm seeing on Instagram or TikTok somebody say, 'Oh my goodness, this faux leather jacket is from M&S and it looks like it's £500 from the runway.' "And what am I doing?

sentences.text: I'm hop, skip, jumping into my car and getting straight to my local M&S to hunt it down," Sian jokes.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "They have embraced young designers like Marco Capaldo, the founder and creative director of 16Arlington," adds Nnadi.
sentences.article_title: From 'fusty' to fashionable - is it cool to wear M&S clothes now?

sentences.text: "And the Aries collab was genius and unexpected - it's a brand that has a lot of fashion kudos and is very British in its aesthetic but represents a younger vision of what British cool looks like," she says.

sentences.text: Clark agrees the brand has "homed in on experts in their craft, rather than partnering with a million different people" like other fashion brands have made the mistake of doing.

sentences.text: She notes their recent partnership with Stormzy's stylist Melissa Holbrook-Akposoe, who goes by Melissa's Wardrobe on social media, as "adding credibility" for younger shoppers.

sentences.text: Chiltern Railways, which was privatised in 1996, has become part of the Great British Railways Chiltern Railways has been brought into public ownership after 30 years as a private company.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: It is the 10th rail company now under the Great British Railways (GBR), the government's programme of public ownership , which it says will save money and improve services.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: Chiltern Railways, which was privatised in 1996, operates services from London Marylebone to Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Warwickshire, as well as destinations in the West Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: The government said the transfer into public ownership would tackle overcrowding by introducing 25 additional daily services from December.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: The start of the first day of public ownership saw some disruption, with Chiltern warning the line between Birmingham and Marylebone , external was "expected to be much busier" due to the late notice of the West Coast Main Line closure affecting services at London Euston.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: The operator said it would run more trains than usual between the stations with significantly enhanced capacity.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: The Department for Transport (DfT) said the additional weekday services under GBR would provide 10,000 extra seats.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: They would include half hourly services during weekdays on the Chiltern Main Line between London and Birmingham, as well as more weekend services.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: Rail minister Lord Peter Hendy met staff at Marylebone Station on Thursday alongside the first Chiltern train in the GBR livery.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: "The most difficult thing on Chiltern is that it's shorter capacity and those extra trains and those extra seats will make a real difference to people travelling on this line up here from Marylebone every day," he said.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: Rail minister Lord Peter Hendy said the government hoped to "build a railway the country can trust and rely on" The rollout of the new trains would also improve accessibility and provide better Wi-Fi on board, the rail operator said.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: From Sunday, passengers whose train had been cancelled can use another operator's service two hours either side of their train to get to their destination at no extra cost, it added.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: Chiltern's interim managing director Tony Baxter said: "Sunday is a significant milestone for Chiltern Railways and we look forward to working together with the wider rail industry to deliver a better railway for everyone in Great Britain." The aim is for GBR to operate all passenger services by the end of 2027.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: Great Western Railway's services will be the next operator to be brought into public ownership, on 13 December.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: Lord Henry said: "Every transfer into public ownership gives us the chance to tackle the bread-and-butter issues people care about – more frequent, comfortable trains that turn up on time.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: "As we set up Great British Railways (GBR), we're putting passengers first.
sentences.article_title: Chiltern Railways renationalised after 30 years

sentences.text: "It will not happen overnight, but we will build a railway the country can trust and rely on and that will create growth, jobs and homes." sentences.text: Deputy leader Daisy Cooper says she has a plan for growth Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper has warned the UK's economic growth is being held back by a "computer says no" approach.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: She unveiled a 30-page growth plan , external aimed at removing barriers to business as part of her speech to the Lib Dem conference in Brighton.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: Cooper, who is also the party's Treasury spokesperson, said too many ideas, start-ups and research started in Britain but ended up being taken overseas.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: She also outlined a new Growth and Defence Partnership with the EU to reverse the economic damage of Brexit, that she claimed is currently costing the UK £90bn a year in lost tax revenue.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: Speaking on stage in Brighton, she said: "We build brilliant start-ups, and watch too many leave to scale somewhere else.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: We produce world-class research, and too little of it becomes a British product." "Britain has the potential," she went on.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: "The system holds it back.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: "This plan tears down the barriers to investment, to innovation, and to skills." Cooper called for the creation of a digital one-stop-shop service for businesses and investors, combining tax, regulatory, legal, Companies House, and general business services.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: Creating this within a new Department for Growth would simplify red tape and help small and medium-sized businesses compete and grow, she said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: Cooper said a new Growth and Defence Partnership with the EU, would be the "single biggest growth lever we could pull" by  deepening ties with Europe.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: "It could turbo-charge our economy and start to reverse the economic damage of Brexit which is currently costing us £90bn a year in lost tax revenue," she said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: New Yorkers, and LinkedIn's Nicole Leverich, share their networking tips For some, networking comes naturally but for others, the thought of approaching someone they don't know and trying to make a professional connection can fill them with dread.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Whether you're looking for your first job, trying to get ahead at work or hoping to change career, building a network can help you find opportunities and make connections.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Networking doesn't have to mean working a room at a formal event - it can happen in person over a coffee at work, through a chance conversation or online, through email and social media.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Just under half (44%) of Gen Z say not having the right network is the biggest barrier to landing an entry-level role, according to research from LinkedIn , external .
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Nicole Leverich, chief communications officer at LinkedIn, shares her top tips on how to network and we took the same question to city workers in New York to find out what has worked for them.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Everyone can start building their network online and "you'd be surprised how many connections you have once you connect with people you went to school with, former professors, people you met through summer jobs, family and friends," says Leverich.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Don't be discouraged if your network is small as "not having a network right now doesn't mean you'll never have a network", she says.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: And not having obvious industry contacts shouldn't put you off.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Leverich grew up in a small town in Oregon and moved to San Francisco after college without knowing anyone who worked in communications.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: In a message you should "reference something they've posted or establish some common ground".
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Make sure your request is "clear and specific" and something they can do in less than five minutes.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: And, most importantly, don't forget to say thank you.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "You'd be surprised by how many people are willing to help, but I get so few thank yous," she says.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "I'm not talking about anything excessive but just a 'thanks' makes you want to help next time." Networking can feel transactional, so to avoid that, try to build relationships before you need something from them, Leverich advises.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: If you know you want to work in a particular industry, "start finding people in that field a year or two before you're looking for a job".
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: When you reach out to them, think about what you can offer them in return.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "If you call me and say you want a job randomly, I'm much less likely to help than if you call and ask for five minutes of advice." You also don't have to start by messaging someone directly, she says.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Instead you could react to a post or drop a comment.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: In-person networking can be more daunting, particularly early in your career, but remember that at a networking event, everyone is there to talk.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: To begin a conversation, start with something simple like complimenting someone's outfit, introducing yourself and asking why they're there, Leverich advises.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: Taylor Crow who works in sales says she's "fairly good" at networking as it was something she prioritised at university.
sentences.article_title: I sent 200 LinkedIn messages and got a job: How to nail networking

sentences.text: "I sent over 200 cold DMs (direct messages) on LinkedIn and reached out to people in the companies I wanted to work at while I was studying." She admits it was "so awkward" but it was something she had to do to land the job she wanted.

sentences.text: "I think it is an important step forward in the industry in terms of really identifying industry norms, and I think that would be beneficial overall," Spiegel told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.text: "We've looked really thoughtfully at the terms." As part of Meta's August settlement , the company said it would implement even more stringent time limits and pay an additional $5.3bn if YouTube and TikTok follow suit.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.text: It has denied any wrongdoing as part of the deal, which will be paid over a 10-year period.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.text: When asked about the idea of a default time limit, Spiegel said: "I think that's a really good example of something that that we'd be willing to implement." But Spiegel did not commit to a timeline on when Snap might take action.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.text: "That's something we've talked about internally," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.text: "We want to figure out how we can be part of the solution," Spiegel added.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.article_title: Snapchat open to putting time limits on teens, boss tells BBC

sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottled offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Mark Carney (left) walks alongside European Parliament President Roberta Metsola (centre) and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen (right) The president of the European Commission has backed proposals for Canada to become the EU's first "associate member".
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Wednesday she wanted to work on "opening the door" for Canada, which would involve closer ties on various key sectors.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: The country currently faces tense relations with the US, compounded by an intensifying dispute over trade.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Insisting it would not be a "partnership against anyone else", Von der Leyen did not mention Donald Trump by name.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Nevertheless the US president threatened to cut trade with the European Union in response to the proposal.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney last week spoke of seeking a "unique alliance" with the EU.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Carney was in attendance at the annual key note speech in Strasbourg, and is due to address the parliament on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Trade talks between Canada and the US collapsed last month, sparking a series of new tariff measures .
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Trump's repeated talk of making Canada a "51st state" has also helped to fuel the feud between the North American neighbours.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: "And we have stood together: on Ukraine, on defence, on raw materials and on supply chains.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Europe and Canada believe in democracy." She added: "Partnerships are a strategic choice for Europe.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: But they also respond to the fracture in the international rules-based system".
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: She did not give specific details on how any Canadian membership would work, but listed manufacturing, technology, artificial intelligence (AI), defence, energy, critical minerals and economic security as key areas for cooperation.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: When asked about the plan, Trump called it "laughable".
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: "If they do that, if I think it's at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe, on many things." He added: "If it's a good intention, that's fine.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: If it's a bad intention, we'll put very heavy tariffs on Europe, which is a possibility." Both von der Leyen and other European leaders have found a reliable ally in Carney as they deal with similar problems.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: In particular, they have faced Trump's aggressive use of tariffs and his threat to annex Greenland which is a sovereign territory of EU member Denmark.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: But "associate membership" of the EU does not currently exist and the process, if agreed, could take years.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Earlier this year, Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz suggested - to a mixed reaction - that Ukraine could be granted this new status.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: In Eastern Europe, Georgia and Moldova are also applying.
sentences.article_title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'

sentences.text: Eric Fawley, from Blackpool, has produced hundreds of drawings since arriving at Greenbanks Care Home in Watford, Hertfordshire, over a year ago, after a fire at his home.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: His drawings and paintings depict the world around him, as well as his former bosses at BT.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: The exhibition was facilitated by the Watford Labour MP Matt Turmaine after he saw Fawley's work at the care home.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: This is one of the few drawings Fawley has produced in colour, as he prefers to sketch in black and white Fawley said he began creating artworks from an early age, encouraged by his mother, a violinist, and his father, a gifted amateur painter.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: His family were unable to support his ambition to attend art school.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: He left school at the age of 14 and worked in a variety of jobs, including electrical work for the famous Blackpool illuminations, before going on to become a Post Office engineer with BT.

sentences.text: Burnham said it "feels very fitting" to welcome Martin as the first international visitor to Number 10 North Ireland's relationship with the UK under Andy Burnham's premiership has got off to a "very good start", Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin has said.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: But he refused to be drawn on how much the issue of Irish unity had featured during their first official meeting at Number 10 North on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The visit came days after US President Donald Trump made comments about supporting a "unified Ireland".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin said the men had a "broad discussion" about upholding the Good Friday Agreement and that they did not get into specifics.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: "It was the first meeting, it went well...
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: I think we have the capacity to make a lot of progress on a lot of issues in the time ahead," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin was the first international leader to visit the government's new headquarters in Manchester, and also visited the Brian Boru Irish Club in Burnham's constituency in Ashton-in-Makerfield.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: On his visit to Northern Ireland last month, Burnham said a border poll was " off the table ", but later said he stood by the Good Friday Agreement.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The taoiseach and prime minister visited the Brian Boru Irish Club in Ashton-in-Makerfield The taoiseach said he and the prime minister had discussed the UK's Troubles legacy legislation in depth, and that he had "stressed the importance" of passing the bill through Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The government is expected to publish details of changes in the middle of next month, with Martin saying both London and Dublin had been working closely on it.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He also said both he and the prime minister wanted to see the power-sharing institutions at Stormont working more effectively, and that the Irish government believes there needs to be reform.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He said Burnham understood the issue and was currently focused on trying to resolve negotiations with the Stormont executive to agree a budget for this year.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Burnham said the relationship between the UK and Ireland matters "on every single level" as he greeted the taoiseach on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The prime minister said they were "working together" to uphold the principles of the peace deal for Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Burnham added that as "co-custodians of the Good Friday Agreement, we are working together to uphold its principles as we approach the 30th anniversary".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The Good Friday Agreement, also known as the Belfast Agreement, was a political deal designed to bring an end to 30 years of violent conflict in Northern Ireland, known as the Troubles.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The taoiseach expressed his sympathies with Burnham following the recent death of his father .
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin said he appreciated the meeting going ahead, telling the prime minister: "I think your sense of duty shines through." The taoiseach said "in a global world marked by uncertainty" it was "important that two close neighbours continue the very strong engagement".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He added: "We are co-guarantors of the Good Friday Agreement.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: We have very significant obligations to mind it and to progress it." Martin said he was also looking forward to discussing "even stronger and closer relationships between the European Union and the United Kingdom, which will be of benefit to the European Union and to Ireland".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Members of Youth Parliament pictured in the House of Commons chamber in February 2025 The UK Youth Parliament is at risk of being axed within months, BBC News has learned, as the government is not committing to funding it any longer.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: The parliament was launched in 2000 to boost interest in politics among young people and has more than 300 elected members aged between 11 and 18.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Once a year, the young politicians are allowed to hold debates in the House of Commons chamber, on a day when MPs are not sitting.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Some MPs and young people say axing it would be a blow for youth democracy, while others say it is not providing value for money.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: The Department of Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), which funds the parliament each year with taxpayer cash, is not committing to giving any more grants to it.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the DCMS praised the youth parliament's "important legacy... giving elected young people a national platform to represent their peers, engage with decision-makers and develop confidence, leadership and skills for life and work".
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: It received £453,000 in taxpayer funding in the last year alone with about £2.4m public money spent on it among other youth initiatives between 2017 and 2024.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: While no final decision has been made on funding beyond March 2027, a government source said: "The government has not committed to continuing the programme in its current form." UK Youth Parliament insiders told the BBC that without government funding, it is likely to close.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: It follows a government review , external published in October last year, which concluded that while the parliament was delivering on its intended goals, only a quarter of young people know about it - and some schools felt "excluded from the process".
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: The government says it is working with young people and youth organisations to design a new scheme that increases their involvement in democracy and decision-making, with further announcements to be made this autumn.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Any new scheme will have a "particular focus on under-represented groups", a government source said.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Bobby Forbes, the recently departed chair of the UK Youth Parliament's Youth Select Committee, which works with officials in Westminster, said it gives teenagers "a direct way to scrutinise government and hold decision-makers to account".
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Bobby Forbes, 18, was a member of the UK Youth Parliament until recently The 18-year-old said scrapping it "would be a huge mistake and detrimental to youth voice across the UK," and it should be allowed to evolve within its current format.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: But Jack Rankin, the Conservative MP for Windsor, said last year it "should not receive taxpayers' money and should not sit in the Chamber of the House of Commons".
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: He has said it should be funded by voluntary donations rather than public money.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: It is understood the funding is spent on the UK Youth Parliament's annual conference, held in Brighton last year, plus travel, communication and support staff.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: The youth parliament is run by the National Youth Agency, but was previously under the British Youth Council which closed amid financial challenges in 2024.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Members are elected every one to two years by voters aged 11 to 18 who live, work or go to school in local authorities.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Similar schemes are held for the devolved Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish parliaments.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Some politicians started their careers in the UK Youth Parliament, including Labour minister Keir Mather who became the youngest MP in 2023 - known as the "baby of the House" - when elected aged 25.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Peter Swallow, the Labour MP for Bracknell in Berkshire who ran for UK Youth Parliament aged 14, told the BBC the organisation has campaigned successfully on issues such as votes for 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: A Bill to lower the voting age from 18 to 16 for all UK elections is currently making its way through Parliament.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: It would be "short-sighted to cut off funding to a scheme" given these developments, Swallow said.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: "With nearly a million young people not in education, employment or training, we should be doing more to engage them, not less," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: He called on the government to set out "a credible replacement" to the Youth Parliament "that reaches young people, reconnects those becoming disengaged and gives the next generation a real stake in our democracy".
sentences.article_title: UK Youth Parliament looks set to be axed

sentences.text: Harrogate and Knaresborough Lib Dem MP Tom Gordon would like to see devolution go further A Liberal Democrat MP has called on Prime Minister Andy Burnham to go further with his devolution plans and give Yorkshire its own parliament.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Harrogate and Knaresborough MP Tom Gordon said too much power was currently in the hands of elected mayors and a Yorkshire parliament would better reflect the region.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Burnham has recently set out plans to give elected mayors more power over planning and tackling fly-tipping and said he would give them a share of income tax and business rates.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: But Gordon told BBC Politics North he believed that giving more money and powers to four separate Yorkshire mayoralties actually deepened divides in the county and a Yorkshire parliament would be "a good thing".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Yorkshire currently has three Labour mayors - Oliver Coppard for South Yorkshire, Tracy Brabin for West Yorkshire and David Skaith for York and North Yorkshire - as well as Luke Campbell, the Reform UK mayor of Hull and East Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: The Lib Dem said that while people had been told the recent local government reorganisation in North Yorkshire would "simplify" the situation, he believed that was not the case.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "We've ended up with a new North Yorkshire Council at a higher tier and a Harrogate town council below it, so we've ended up with two tiers.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: In fact, there's a third tier when you throw in the regional mayor," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "So we've ended up with more tiers, but those powers have been moved upwards rather than down to people.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "I think we owe it to have everyone have a seat at that table, not just all that power put in one person's hands." Gordon said he believed a Yorkshire parliament was the way forward "if it's good enough for Scotland, if it's good enough for Wales, if it's good enough for London".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "We should have a model where we have broader people elected to it who can feed in all those issues into a Yorkshire-wide parliament.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: That, to me, is only a good thing," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: The idea of a Yorkshire parliament has previously been advocated by the Yorkshire Party.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Since 2014, the party has argued that it would create a more "engaged, democratic society".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Meanwhile, when devolution deals were first being discussed, a proposal was put forward for one mayor for all of Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: The so-called "One Yorkshire" plan was backed by 18 of the region's 20 local councils, while Sheffield and Rotherham opted for a separate South Yorkshire solution.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: However, the then Conservative Communities Secretary James Brokenshire rejected the proposal and said the plan did "not meet our criteria" .
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Deals were later done for the four counties within Yorkshire In a speech earlier this year, Burnham said decision-making needed to be "pushed to regions and local communities" , adding that it would see "good growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: David Skaith says Yorkshire's mayors work "collectively" Responding to Gordon's comments, Skaith said the Greater Manchester and Liverpool City Region, which has had devolved powers for longer, had worked "really well".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: But Skaith also said he believed that all views were represented within the current system.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "It's not just four mayors who sit in Yorkshire, all our combined authorities are made up of those local authorities as well," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "So, I'm not making decisions sat in York and North Yorkshire on my own.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: It's in partnership with the two local authorities." Skaith pointed to the so-called "White Rose Agreement", signed by himself and the mayors of South and West Yorkshire, pledging to work closer on things like transport.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: “Rail is a classic case - Northern Powerhouse Rail - where we got particularly the working around York station and the wider area of North Yorkshire," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch the moment Kate Wills found out she would be able to access Enhertu Patients in England with a specific type of incurable breast cancer can now access a life-extending drug on the NHS, two years after it was deemed too expensive by a health body.

sentences.text: Enhertu can give patients almost seven extra months to live on average - with some living up to three years longer.
sentences.article_title: New hope for breast cancer patients as life-extending drug now on NHS in England

sentences.text: Women in Scotland have had access to the drug on the NHS since 2023, and it is available in 26 other European countries.
sentences.article_title: New hope for breast cancer patients as life-extending drug now on NHS in England

sentences.text: Charities and patients have campaigned for it to be more widely available since 2024, when the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) said Enhertu was not good value for money.
sentences.article_title: New hope for breast cancer patients as life-extending drug now on NHS in England

sentences.text: From Thursday, doctors in England are now able to prescribe it, with Wales expected to follow shortly.
sentences.article_title: New hope for breast cancer patients as life-extending drug now on NHS in England

sentences.article_title: New hope for breast cancer patients as life-extending drug now on NHS in England

sentences.text: "When I say, 'we consultants', I am responsible as well and if my other consultant colleagues didn't go to the police, I should have." The Thirlwall Inquiry was launched after former nurse Letby was convicted in 2023, and the final report was published on Tuesday.

sentences.text: Reflecting on the findings for the first time, Gibbs said: "I wasn't expecting it to be an easy read and it certainly isn't.
